title: Homeland Security and Public Safety
gist: A RAND topic index page for Homeland Security and Public Safety, listing 7,828 results and surfacing its most recent outputs from late August to September 2026. The recency list is itself a signal of RAND's current research agenda: AI-enabled biosecurity risk, AI model distillation and U.S. frontier-model advantage, AI in disaster response and supply chains, psychedelics policy, opioid treatment, gun ownership and criminal justice capacity.

insights.claim: RAND's homeland security research portfolio spans border and port security, critical infrastructure protection, cybersecurity, disaster management and recovery, and Arctic policy, while its public safety work covers drug policy, emergency preparedness, crime and school safety.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Maps where an influential U.S. policy shop concentrates analytic firepower, which tends to precede regulatory and appropriations attention.
insights.locator: RAND conducts research and analysis on homeland security issues

insights.claim: The homeland security and public safety topic area carries 7,828 published results, indicating a very deep institutional back catalog in this domain.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Scale of prior work signals durable institutional authority in homeland security policy debates.

themes.theme: AI risk moves to the center of the security agenda

insights.claim: RAND argues AI can now design viruses and that the risk of engineered viral bioweapons is growing, calling for a layered, resilient system of defense built during the current preparation window.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: A leading policy institution framing AI biosecurity as urgent raises the probability of model-access and biological-synthesis screening regulation touching AI labs and synthesis providers.
insights.quote: As AI advances, the risk of engineered viral bioweapons is growing. The window to prepare is now

insights.claim: RAND treats AI model distillation - training new models on the outputs of more capable ones - as a threat to U.S. frontier model advantage, and argues new policy tools should augment technical countermeasures such as raising costs or degrading output quality.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Policy interest in blocking distillation is a potential regulatory moat for U.S. frontier labs and a constraint on cheap fast-follower model developers.
insights.quote: could affect U.S. frontier model advantage
insights.locator: Countering Model Distillation: Limits and Alternatives

insights.claim: RAND has examined how embedding AI in logistics, transport and warehousing supply chains changes operational reliance, resilience and insurance risk.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Flags an emerging underwriting category: AI operational dependency as an insurable and priceable risk in logistics.
insights.locator: Operational reliance on AI in supply chains and emerging insurance risks

insights.claim: RAND frames AI as a potential relief valve for emergency managers facing disasters that are more frequent, more severe and more costly.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Public-sector disaster response is an under-covered AI procurement channel with climate-driven budget growth behind it.
insights.quote: Disasters are more frequent, more severe, and more costly.
insights.locator: When Disaster Strikes, Could AI Help?

insights.claim: RAND publicly pressed OpenAI to provide proof behind its claim that ChatGPT is safer for teens, signaling institutional skepticism toward vendor-stated AI safety assurances.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Demands for evidentiary proof of consumer AI safety claims foreshadow disclosure or audit requirements for consumer-facing model providers.
insights.quote: OpenAI Says ChatGPT Is Safer for Teens. Now It Needs to Show Proof.
insights.locator: OpenAI Says ChatGPT Is Safer for Teens

themes.theme: Drug policy and public health pipeline

insights.claim: RAND is convening work on the state of psychedelics in America covering usage, public views and the range of policy options, indicating psychedelics policy is moving into mainstream analysis.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Mainstream policy analysis typically precedes regulatory liberalization - relevant to the psychedelics therapeutics pipeline.
insights.locator: The State of Psychedelics in America

insights.claim: RAND flags that millions of U.S. adults use Amanita muscaria mushrooms, which are pharmacologically unlike other psychoactive mushrooms and pose distinct questions for consumers and policymakers.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: An unregulated consumer category at scale is a classic precursor to enforcement action or a new regulatory regime.
insights.quote: Millions of U.S. adults use Amanita muscaria mushrooms
insights.locator: Millions of U.S. adults use Amanita muscaria

insights.claim: RAND adapted an opioid use disorder cascade-of-care framework to the constraints of electronic health record data in a large municipal health system in order to identify patients at risk of treatment discontinuity.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: EHR-based risk stratification for opioid treatment retention is an operational hook for health-system analytics vendors.
insights.locator: Framework for the Opioid Use Disorder Cascade of Care

insights.claim: RAND evaluated the Los Angeles County Public Defender's Case Complexity System and the office's capacity to represent clients amid growing case complexity and resource constraints.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Documented public-defense capacity strain in the largest U.S. county is a leading indicator of court backlog and justice-system funding fights.
insights.locator: Los Angeles County Public Defender Attorney Workload Study

insights.claim: Twenty-five years after the September 11 attacks, RAND experts are revisiting soft-target protection, the role of the TSA and risks from emerging technologies, indicating the homeland security framework is being re-litigated rather than settled.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: A reopened post-9/11 security consensus creates room for reallocation of aviation and soft-target security spending.
insights.locator: 25 Years After 9/11: Lessons for Securing the Homeland
